question: New shameful agreement: a further EUR 7 400 million to outsource border control and deepen the Fortress Europe model

On Sunday, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Egyptian President al-Sisi together signed an economic aid agreement for Egypt worth over EUR 7 400 million. Including loans, donations and concessions, its aim is for Egypt to stop migrants, including potential asylum seekers, from arriving in EU territory.

As usual under von der Leyen’s presidency, the EU is handing over billions of euros to third countries to outsource migration control so that it can look the other way if human rights violations are committed against migrants on their way to Europe. And, once again, under formulas that avoid any scrutiny by the European Parliament. 1.
What guarantees does the Commission have to ensure that these funds are not used for practices contrary to international law and EU legislation on asylum and migration?
What mechanisms for economic control, transparency and respect for human rights in the use of the funds does the Commission intend to include in the agreement?

Can the Commission say how many billions of euros the EU has committed to such agreements to prevent the arrival of migrants and asylum seekers by externalising migration control and building a Fortress Europe?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.7.2024) The Commission works with Member States in a Team Europe approach to deepen comprehensive partnerships with third countries based on mutual interests.

Tailor-made partnerships that reflect shared goals - such as stability and security; economic development and reforms; investment, trade and employment; energy; green and digital transitions; peopleto-people contacts, migration and mobility - can deepen relations and a shared strategic vision.

The EU and Egypt took their cooperation to the level of a Strategic and Comprehensive Partnership, launched with the signature of the Joint Declaration on 17 March 20241, with the aim of deepening their shared stability, peace and prosperity. The partnership covers six key pillars: political relations; economic stability; trade and investment; migration and mobility; security and demography; and human capital.

A financial and investment support package of EUR 7.4 billion for Egypt will underpin the Partnership. It will consist of short and longerterm support, covering for the period 2024-2027. The respect and protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms is a key element in the EU cooperation with Egypt.

In the Joint Declaration, Egypt and the EU reaffirmed continued work on their commitments to further promote democracy, fundamental freedoms and human rights, gender equality and equal opportunities, as agreed in the EU-Egypt Partnership priorities.

The EU reconfirmed that it stands ready to assist Egypt in the implementation of its national strategy for human rights in alignment with the provisions of the Association Agreement2 and the Partnership Priorities for 2021-2027. The EU will continue to assess the situation on the ground.
On migration, the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument will support its implementation with EUR 200 million.

In line with the holistic approach to migration laid down in the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum3, EU financial support to Egypt on migration-related programs will cover, including legal migration pathways and mobility schemes, tackling the root causes of irregular migration, combating smuggling of migrants and trafficking in persons, strengthening border management, and ensuring dignified and sustainable return and reintegration.
The Commission monitors its programmes through regular reports from implementing partners, external evaluation, verification missions and specific results-oriented monitoring exercises.
